writeup.headline: Eli Lilly rates Strong Buy on rapid growth, high gross margins, strong trend and raised guidance.
writeup.thesis: Lilly scores 84, a Strong Buy, driven mainly by a very strong price trend (97) and high quality (94). The shares are 18.4% above their 200-day average, 42.8 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days and only 1.4% below their 52-week high. Quality rests on a gross margin of 83.4%, stock-based pay of 0.8% of revenue and diluted share count down 0.7% year on year. Growth scores 77 on TTM revenue growth of 49.6%, though growth slowed by 7.9 pp from the previous quarter. News is supportive (68): Lilly raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $91–92B for the third time this year. Balance sheet and valuation had no score here. P/S of 15.2x is high in absolute terms but near the middle of its own history.
key_risks: Growth is decelerating: latest-quarter revenue growth of 47.7% year on year, with growth slowed by 7.9 pp from the previous quarter.
P/S of 15.2x is high in absolute terms, leaving little room for disappointment.
Competition in obesity drugs, including Novo's cheaper self-pay pricing and the Foundayo pill launch missing estimates.
The GLP-1 product-liability MDL and copycat retatrutide sellers are ongoing legal background risks.
After a strong run (shares up 44.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago), the price is extended at 8.1% above its 50-day average.
what_would_change: The score is 5 points above the Buy band (below 80); a further slowdown in revenue growth or a weaker trend score could tip it down.
A pullback that erodes the 97 trend score, such as the price falling back toward its 200-day average, would weigh on the rating.
Negative guidance or competitive news, such as share loss to Novo or pricing pressure, would cut the 68 news score.
Once scored, the balance sheet and valuation factors could move the composite either way.
